rules.title: User profile
rules.summary: Your profile: personal folders, app settings (AppData) and tool data
rules.whatItIs: The home folder of one account: Documents, Downloads, Pictures and the other personal folders, the hidden AppData folder with app settings and caches, and dot-folders created by developer tools.
rules.whyBig: Personal files plus the caches and data of every app this account uses.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting the whole profile removes the account's files and settings and breaks its sign-in.
rules.saferAlternative: Look inside: personal folders are yours to judge, and caches in AppData are explained one by one.

rules.title: AppData (app settings and data)
rules.summary: Hidden folder where apps keep settings, caches and data for this account
rules.whatItIs: Hidden folder with three parts: Local (data that stays on this PC, including caches), LocalLow (data of apps running with low permissions) and Roaming (settings that can follow the account).
rules.whyBig: Browser profiles, game launchers, developer tools and app caches; often tens of GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Every app loses its settings and data for this account, and some per-user installed apps stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Clean the cache folders inside, which are marked individually.

rules.title: AppData\Local
rules.summary: Per-user app data that stays on this PC: caches, local installs, app state
rules.whatItIs: Data that apps keep for this account on this PC only: caches, temporary files, browser profiles, Store app data and programs installed per user (Programs).
rules.whyBig: Usually the largest part of a profile's app data, because caches, shader caches and per-user installs live here.
rules.ifDeleted: Apps lose their data and per-user installed programs stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Clean the subfolders marked SAFE; check the others one by one.

rules.title: AppData\Roaming
rules.summary: App settings and data for this account (can roam with the account)
rules.whatItIs: Settings and data that apps store per account; in a domain with roaming profiles it follows the user between PCs. Many apps also put caches or even program files here.
rules.whyBig: Some apps keep caches, downloads or whole installations here (for example Electron apps, mod managers and game launchers).
rules.ifDeleted: Apps lose their settings and data, and apps installed here stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Check the subfolders one by one.

rules.title: AppData\LocalLow
rules.summary: Data of sandboxed apps and many games, including Unity game saves
rules.whatItIs: Data folder for apps that run with low integrity (sandboxed browsers and plug-ins). Games built with Unity store their saves and settings here under <Company>\<Game>.
rules.whyBig: Game saves are small, but some games and apps cache downloaded content or logs here.
rules.ifDeleted: Games lose their saves and settings; apps lose their data.
rules.saferAlternative: Check each company or game folder before deleting it.

rules.title: Low-integrity temporary files
rules.summary: Temporary files of sandboxed apps; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Temporary folder for apps running with low integrity.
rules.whyBig: Leftover temporary files from apps and games.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; files in use are locked.

rules.title: Your temporary files
rules.summary: Temporary files of your apps and installers; safe to clear, files in use are skipped
rules.whatItIs: Your account's temporary folder (%TEMP%). Apps, installers and updaters put working files here and are supposed to remove them.
rules.whyBig: Installers extract packages here and many apps never clean up, so it often holds several GB of old extracted setups, logs and downloads.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; files in use are locked and stay. A few apps keep recovery files here (Blender saves quit.blend and autosaves to the temp folder by default), so check for those if you rely on them.
rules.saferAlternative: Use Storage settings > Temporary files, or delete items older than a few days.

rules.title: winget download cache
rules.summary: Installers downloaded by winget; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Installers that the Windows Package Manager (winget) downloaded to install or upgrade apps.
rules.whyBig: Each installed or upgraded package leaves its installer here.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; winget downloads installers again when needed.

rules.title: Internet cache (WinINet)
rules.summary: Web cache of Windows components, Office and older apps; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: The Windows internet cache used by Internet Explorer mode, Office, Outlook (attachment previews in Content.Outlook) and apps that use the Windows web stack.
rules.whyBig: Office and apps that download content through Windows can leave hundreds of MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; content is downloaded again. Close Outlook before clearing Content.Outlook, which also holds attachments you opened.
rules.saferAlternative: Storage settings > Temporary files > Temporary Internet Files.

rules.title: Explorer thumbnail and icon caches
rules.summary: Thumbnail and icon caches of File Explorer; rebuilt automatically
rules.whatItIs: File Explorer's thumbcache_*.db and iconcache_*.db databases with cached thumbnails and icons.
rules.whyBig: Browsing large photo and video folders in thumbnail view makes it grow, sometimes to 1 GB or more.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; thumbnails are recreated when you open folders. Files in use by Explorer are locked.
rules.saferAlternative: Storage settings > Temporary files > Thumbnails.

rules.title: Legacy icon cache
rules.summary: Old-style Explorer icon cache; rebuilt automatically
rules.whatItIs: Icon cache file kept by File Explorer for compatibility.
rules.whyBig: A few MB at most.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; Explorer rebuilds it.

rules.title: Windows web cache database
rules.summary: Database of the Windows web stack (history, cookies); locked while in use
rules.whatItIs: WebCacheV01.dat and its logs, used by Internet Explorer mode, Explorer and other Windows components to track web history, cookies and downloads.
rules.whyBig: Usually tens of MB; it can occasionally grow large.
rules.ifDeleted: The files are locked by Windows tasks while you are signed in; forcing removal can reset cookies and history of components that use it.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear it through Internet Options > General > Browsing history > Delete.

rules.title: Your installed fonts
rules.summary: Fonts installed only for your account
rules.whatItIs: Fonts installed with 'Install' (not 'Install for all users') land here.
rules.whyBig: Font families from design tools and packs can be tens of MB each.
rules.ifDeleted: The fonts disappear from your apps, and documents using them fall back to other fonts.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove fonts you no longer need in Settings > Personalization > Fonts.

rules.title: App crash dumps
rules.summary: Crash dumps of your apps; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Memory dumps written by Windows Error Reporting when an app you run crashes.
rules.whyBig: Some apps write full dumps of hundreds of MB; repeated crashes fill it quickly.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; those crashes can no longer be analysed.

rules.title: DirectX shader cache
rules.summary: Compiled DirectX shaders for games and apps; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Shaders compiled by Direct3D for your graphics card, so games and apps do not have to compile them at every start.
rules.whyBig: Every game adds its compiled shaders, often hundreds of MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the next launch of each game recompiles shaders, which can cause longer loading or brief stutter.
rules.saferAlternative: Storage settings > Temporary files > DirectX Shader Cache.

rules.title: Microsoft app data (Local)
rules.summary: Data of Windows and Microsoft apps for your account: Edge, Office, OneDrive, caches
rules.whatItIs: Per-user data of Windows components and Microsoft apps: Edge profiles, OneDrive, Office caches, Visual Studio, Windows caches and app execution aliases.
rules.whyBig: Edge profiles and Office or Teams caches are usually the largest parts.
rules.ifDeleted: Windows features and Microsoft apps lose their data; some stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Clean the cache folders inside, which are marked individually.

rules.title: Windows per-user data (Local)
rules.summary: Windows data for your account: caches, history, notifications, fonts
rules.whatItIs: Per-user Windows data: Explorer caches, the internet cache, notifications, per-user fonts, the class registry hive (UsrClass.dat) and more.
rules.whyBig: Thumbnail and internet caches are the usual large parts.
rules.ifDeleted: Windows features break for your account; UsrClass.dat is part of your registry.
rules.saferAlternative: Clean the cache folders inside, which are marked individually.

rules.title: App execution aliases
rules.summary: Zero-byte command aliases for Store apps (winget, python, wt); takes no space
rules.whatItIs: Small links that let you start packaged apps from a command line, such as winget.exe, wt.exe or the python.exe alias. This folder is on your PATH.
rules.whyBig: The entries are zero-byte reparse points; they take no real space.
rules.ifDeleted: Commands such as winget and wt stop working from terminals.
rules.saferAlternative: Manage aliases in Settings > Apps > Advanced app settings > App execution aliases.

rules.title: Saved credentials (Local)
rules.summary: Encrypted saved credentials of Credential Manager; tiny, never delete
rules.whatItIs: Encrypted credentials stored by Windows Credential Manager for this account.
rules.whyBig: A few KB.
rules.ifDeleted: Saved passwords for network shares, apps and services are lost.

rules.title: Windows Vault (Local)
rules.summary: Encrypted web and app credentials of Windows; tiny, never delete
rules.whatItIs: Windows Vault storage for web and app credentials saved through Credential Manager.
rules.whyBig: A few KB.
rules.ifDeleted: Saved web and app credentials are lost.

rules.title: Microsoft data (Roaming)
rules.summary: Windows and Office settings for your account, including encryption keys
rules.whatItIs: Per-account settings of Windows and Microsoft apps: Start menu shortcuts, recent items, Office templates, and the keys that protect your saved passwords (Protect, Crypto, Credentials).
rules.whyBig: Usually small; classic Teams and Office add-ins can add caches.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting it can make every password saved with Windows data protection unreadable (browser and Wi-Fi passwords, Credential Manager).
rules.saferAlternative: Leave it; clean individual caches inside only.

rules.title: Data protection master keys (DPAPI)
rules.summary: Keys that decrypt your saved passwords; tiny, never delete
rules.whatItIs: Master keys of the Windows Data Protection API. Browsers, Wi-Fi, Credential Manager and many apps encrypt saved secrets with them.
rules.whyBig: A few KB.
rules.ifDeleted: Saved passwords and encrypted app data of this account become permanently unreadable.

rules.title: Certificate private keys
rules.summary: Private keys of your certificates; tiny, never delete
rules.whatItIs: Private keys of certificates installed for this account (for example for VPN, email signing or code signing).
rules.whyBig: A few KB.
rules.ifDeleted: Certificates lose their private keys and stop working for sign-in, signing or encryption.

rules.title: Saved credentials (Roaming)
rules.summary: Encrypted saved credentials of Credential Manager; tiny, never delete
rules.whatItIs: Encrypted credentials stored by Windows Credential Manager for this account.
rules.whyBig: A few KB.
rules.ifDeleted: Saved passwords for network shares, apps and services are lost.

rules.title: Your certificate store
rules.summary: Certificates installed for your account; tiny, never delete
rules.whatItIs: The per-user certificate store (personal certificates, trusted roots you added).
rules.whyBig: A few KB to a few MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Certificates you installed disappear; sign-in, VPN and signing that rely on them fail.

rules.title: Your Start menu shortcuts
rules.summary: Start menu shortcuts installed for your account
rules.whatItIs: Shortcuts that per-user installed programs put in your Start menu.
rules.whyBig: Tiny; shortcuts only.
rules.ifDeleted: Programs disappear from the Start menu but stay installed.

rules.title: Compatibility link: Application Data
rules.summary: Compatibility link for older programs; takes no disk space
rules.whatItIs: A junction (folder link) that Windows keeps so programs written for older Windows versions find their files. It points to AppData\Roaming.
rules.whyBig: It takes no space; the files it points to are counted in their real location.
rules.ifDeleted: Older programs that still use this path fail. The data itself is not affected, so there is nothing to gain.

rules.title: Compatibility link: Local Settings
rules.summary: Compatibility link for older programs; takes no disk space
rules.whatItIs: A junction (folder link) that Windows keeps so programs written for older Windows versions find their files. It points to AppData\Local.
rules.whyBig: It takes no space; the files it points to are counted in their real location.
rules.ifDeleted: Older programs that still use this path fail. The data itself is not affected, so there is nothing to gain.

rules.title: Compatibility link: My Documents
rules.summary: Compatibility link for older programs; takes no disk space
rules.whatItIs: A junction (folder link) that Windows keeps so programs written for older Windows versions find their files. It points to Documents.
rules.whyBig: It takes no space; the files it points to are counted in their real location.
rules.ifDeleted: Older programs that still use this path fail. The data itself is not affected, so there is nothing to gain.

rules.title: Compatibility link: Local\Application Data
rules.summary: Compatibility link for older programs; takes no disk space
rules.whatItIs: A junction (folder link) that Windows keeps so programs written for older Windows versions find their files. It points to AppData\Local.
rules.whyBig: It takes no space; the files it points to are counted in their real location.
rules.ifDeleted: Older programs that still use this path fail. The data itself is not affected, so there is nothing to gain.

rules.title: Documents
rules.summary: Your documents; apps and games also save files here
rules.whatItIs: Your Documents folder. Many apps and games also save projects, settings and saves here (for example My Games, Visual Studio projects, Zoom recordings).
rules.whyBig: Whatever you and your apps saved; game saves, recordings and projects can be large.
rules.ifDeleted: Your files in it are gone. They go to the Recycle Bin only if you recycle instead of deleting permanently.
rules.saferAlternative: Sort by size and look at the largest items; move what you want to keep to another drive or cloud storage.

rules.title: Downloads
rules.summary: Files you downloaded; old installers and archives often pile up
rules.whatItIs: Default folder for files downloaded by browsers and apps.
rules.whyBig: Installers, archives, ISO images and videos accumulate here and are rarely cleaned up.
rules.ifDeleted: Your files in it are gone. They go to the Recycle Bin only if you recycle instead of deleting permanently.
rules.saferAlternative: Sort by size and look at the largest items; move what you want to keep to another drive or cloud storage.

rules.title: Desktop
rules.summary: Files and shortcuts on your desktop
rules.whatItIs: The files and shortcuts shown on your desktop.
rules.whyBig: Whatever was saved to the desktop.
rules.ifDeleted: Your files in it are gone. They go to the Recycle Bin only if you recycle instead of deleting permanently.
rules.saferAlternative: Sort by size and look at the largest items; move what you want to keep to another drive or cloud storage.

rules.title: Pictures
rules.summary: Your photos, screenshots and images
rules.whatItIs: Your Pictures folder, including Screenshots and Camera Roll.
rules.whyBig: Photo libraries and screenshots grow over the years; RAW photos are tens of MB each.
rules.ifDeleted: Your files in it are gone. They go to the Recycle Bin only if you recycle instead of deleting permanently.
rules.saferAlternative: Sort by size and look at the largest items; move what you want to keep to another drive or cloud storage.

rules.title: Videos
rules.summary: Your videos and screen recordings
rules.whatItIs: Your Videos folder. Xbox Game Bar (Captures), OBS and other recorders save here by default.
rules.whyBig: Screen and gameplay recordings are often several GB each.
rules.ifDeleted: Your files in it are gone. They go to the Recycle Bin only if you recycle instead of deleting permanently.
rules.saferAlternative: Sort by size and look at the largest items; move what you want to keep to another drive or cloud storage.

rules.title: Music
rules.summary: Your music and audio files
rules.whatItIs: Your Music folder.
rules.whyBig: Music libraries, recordings and audio projects.
rules.ifDeleted: Your files in it are gone. They go to the Recycle Bin only if you recycle instead of deleting permanently.
rules.saferAlternative: Sort by size and look at the largest items; move what you want to keep to another drive or cloud storage.

rules.title: Saved Games
rules.summary: Game saves and settings
rules.whatItIs: Folder where many games store saves, profiles and settings.
rules.whyBig: Saves are usually small; some games also keep replays or screenshots here.
rules.ifDeleted: Your files in it are gone. They go to the Recycle Bin only if you recycle instead of deleting permanently.
rules.saferAlternative: Sort by size and look at the largest items; move what you want to keep to another drive or cloud storage.

rules.title: Favorites
rules.summary: Internet Explorer favorites (legacy)
rules.whatItIs: Favorites (bookmarks) of Internet Explorer and apps that use them.
rules.whyBig: Usually tiny.
rules.ifDeleted: Your files in it are gone. They go to the Recycle Bin only if you recycle instead of deleting permanently.
rules.saferAlternative: Sort by size and look at the largest items; move what you want to keep to another drive or cloud storage.

rules.title: Game Bar captures
rules.summary: Clips and screenshots from Xbox Game Bar
rules.whatItIs: Recordings and screenshots made with Xbox Game Bar (Win+Alt+R, Win+Alt+PrtScn).
rules.whyBig: Gameplay clips are large, and 'record what happened' can save many of them.
rules.ifDeleted: Your files in it are gone. They go to the Recycle Bin only if you recycle instead of deleting permanently.
rules.saferAlternative: Sort by size and look at the largest items; move what you want to keep to another drive or cloud storage.

rules.title: OneDrive
rules.summary: Your OneDrive files; online-only files show their size but use no disk
rules.whatItIs: Your OneDrive folder, synced with the cloud. With Files On-Demand, files can be online-only (cloud icon), locally available, or always kept on this device.
rules.whyBig: The size shown here counts online-only files at their full size even though they take no disk space; only locally available files really use space.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting files here deletes them from OneDrive and every synced device too (they stay in the OneDrive recycle bin for a while).
rules.saferAlternative: To free space without deleting, right-click a folder > Free up space, or turn on Storage Sense to make unused files online-only.

rules.title: OneDrive for work or school
rules.summary: Work or school OneDrive; online-only files show their size but use no disk
rules.whatItIs: Your work or school OneDrive folder, synced with your organization's cloud. Files can be online-only, locally available or always kept on this device.
rules.whyBig: Online-only files are counted at full size although they use no disk; only locally available files really use space.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting files here deletes them from the organization's OneDrive as well.
rules.saferAlternative: Right-click a folder > Free up space to make it online-only instead of deleting.

rules.title: OneDrive app
rules.summary: The OneDrive app, its logs and sync settings for your account
rules.whatItIs: Program files of OneDrive when installed per user, plus its logs and sync settings.
rules.whyBig: Each update keeps a version folder for a while; logs are usually modest.
rules.ifDeleted: OneDrive stops syncing; files already in your OneDrive folder stay.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall or reset OneDrive from Installed apps if you do not use it.

rules.title: Store app data
rules.summary: Data of Microsoft Store and packaged apps, one folder per app
rules.whatItIs: Every packaged app (Store apps and parts of Windows) has a folder here with LocalState, LocalCache, TempState, RoamingState and Settings.
rules.whyBig: Messengers, media apps and games with local downloads or caches can each use GBs.
rules.ifDeleted: The app loses its data and settings and may stop working until it is reset or reinstalled.
rules.saferAlternative: Use Settings > Apps > Installed apps > (app) > Advanced options > Reset to clear an app's data properly.

rules.title: Store app temporary files
rules.summary: Temporary files of a Store app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: A packaged app's temporary folder, which Windows may clear at any time.
rules.whyBig: Apps that process media or downloads can leave files here.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; quit the app first.

rules.title: Store app web cache
rules.summary: Web cache of a Store app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: The internet cache of a packaged app's sandbox.
rules.whyBig: Apps that display web content cache images and pages here.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; content is downloaded again.

rules.title: Store app sandbox temporary files
rules.summary: Temporary files in a Store app's sandbox; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Temporary folder inside a packaged app's sandbox (AppContainer).
rules.whyBig: Leftover temporary files of the app.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; quit the app first.

rules.title: Store app local cache
rules.summary: Store app data that is not backed up; despite the name, not always a cache
rules.whatItIs: A packaged app's LocalCache folder. Some apps keep real caches here, but others store real data, for example the Microsoft Store version of Python keeps pip-installed packages here.
rules.whyBig: Media and messenger apps cache downloads here.
rules.ifDeleted: Depends on the app: caches are rebuilt, but installed packages or offline content are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Prefer the app's own 'clear cache' option or Reset in Settings.

rules.title: Store app local data
rules.summary: The Store app's own local data (databases, downloads, settings)
rules.whatItIs: A packaged app's main data folder: its databases, downloaded content and local settings.
rules.whyBig: Messengers, note apps and media apps store their libraries and databases here.
rules.ifDeleted: The app loses its local data, such as chat history, downloaded media or offline content.
rules.saferAlternative: Reset the app from Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Advanced options if you want to start over.

rules.title: Microsoft Teams cache
rules.summary: Cache of the new Microsoft Teams; safe to clear while Teams is closed
rules.whatItIs: Cache and local state of the new Teams app. Microsoft's own troubleshooting steps clear this folder.
rules.whyBig: Teams caches images, files, web resources and logs, often 1 GB or more.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost on the server; Teams downloads what it needs and may ask you to sign in again. Quit Teams first.
rules.saferAlternative: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Microsoft Teams > Advanced options > Reset does the same.

rules.title: Microsoft Teams (new) data
rules.summary: Data of the new Microsoft Teams app
rules.whatItIs: Local data of the new Teams client (the packaged app that replaced classic Teams).
rules.whyBig: Its cache (LocalCache\Microsoft\MSTeams) is the large part.
rules.ifDeleted: Teams loses its local state and signs you out; chats and files stay in the cloud.
rules.saferAlternative: Use Reset in Settings rather than deleting the folder.

rules.title: WhatsApp Desktop data
rules.summary: WhatsApp Desktop: local chat database and downloaded media
rules.whatItIs: Local data of WhatsApp Desktop: the local message database, downloaded photos, videos and documents, and caches.
rules.whyBig: Media you receive in busy chats and groups is downloaded here and adds up to many GB.
rules.ifDeleted: You are logged out and media that is no longer on your phone may be lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove media per chat in WhatsApp (Settings > Storage), or turn off automatic media download.

rules.title: Spotify (Store version) data
rules.summary: Spotify data: streaming cache and downloaded songs
rules.whatItIs: Local data of the Microsoft Store version of Spotify, including its streaming cache and songs downloaded for offline listening.
rules.whyBig: The cache can grow to several GB, plus any downloaded playlists.
rules.ifDeleted: You are signed out, offline downloads are lost and the cache is rebuilt while streaming.
rules.saferAlternative: In Spotify, use Settings > Storage to clear the cache or remove downloads.

rules.title: Telegram Desktop (Store) data
rules.summary: Telegram Desktop: session data and media cache
rules.whatItIs: Local data of the Microsoft Store version of Telegram Desktop: your session and the cache of media you viewed.
rules.whyBig: Media from channels and groups is cached and can grow to many GB.
rules.ifDeleted: You are logged out of this device; cloud chats stay, but cached media must be downloaded again.
rules.saferAlternative: In Telegram, use Settings > Advanced > Manage local storage to clear the cache or set a limit.

rules.title: Python (Microsoft Store) data
rules.summary: Microsoft Store Python: packages installed with pip --user live here
rules.whatItIs: Data of the Microsoft Store version of Python. Packages installed with 'pip install --user' and their scripts live in LocalCache\local-packages.
rules.whyBig: Machine learning and data science packages can be GBs.
rules.ifDeleted: Installed user packages disappear and scripts that need them fail.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove packages with 'pip uninstall', or reset the Python app in Settings.

rules.title: NVIDIA user data
rules.summary: NVIDIA driver data for your account, mainly shader caches
rules.whatItIs: Data kept by the NVIDIA graphics driver for your account, mostly the DirectX and OpenGL shader caches.
rules.whyBig: Shader caches grow with every game you play.
rules.ifDeleted: The caches are rebuilt; games may stutter or load longer at first.

rules.title: NVIDIA DirectX shader cache
rules.summary: Compiled DirectX shaders from the NVIDIA driver; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Shaders the NVIDIA driver compiled for DirectX games.
rules.whyBig: Each game adds compiled shaders; the driver keeps the cache up to a size limit set in the NVIDIA Control Panel.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; games recompile shaders on their next launch, which can cause longer loading or stutter at first.
rules.saferAlternative: Change 'Shader Cache Size' in NVIDIA Control Panel > Manage 3D settings to limit it.

rules.title: NVIDIA OpenGL/Vulkan shader cache
rules.summary: Compiled OpenGL and Vulkan shaders from the NVIDIA driver; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Shaders the NVIDIA driver compiled for OpenGL and Vulkan apps and games.
rules.whyBig: Each game and 3D app adds compiled shaders.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; shaders are recompiled, which can cause stutter at first.

rules.title: NVIDIA shader caches (per driver)
rules.summary: Shader caches of newer NVIDIA drivers; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Newer NVIDIA drivers keep their DirectX and OpenGL shader caches here, separated by driver version.
rules.whyBig: Each game adds compiled shaders, and caches of older driver versions may remain.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; games recompile shaders on their next launch, with longer loading or stutter at first.

rules.title: NVIDIA app data
rules.summary: Data of the NVIDIA app or GeForce Experience and NVIDIA SDK components
rules.whatItIs: Per-user data of NVIDIA software: the NVIDIA app or GeForce Experience, overlay and SDK components used by games.
rules.whyBig: Usually modest; logs and downloaded components can grow.
rules.ifDeleted: NVIDIA software loses its settings; games using NVIDIA SDK features may recreate their data.

rules.title: AMD user data
rules.summary: AMD Software data for your account, including shader caches
rules.whatItIs: Data kept by AMD Software (Adrenalin) and the AMD graphics driver: settings, logs and shader caches.
rules.whyBig: Shader caches grow with every game you play.
rules.ifDeleted: Caches are rebuilt; AMD Software may lose its settings.

rules.title: AMD DirectX shader cache
rules.summary: Compiled DirectX shaders from the AMD driver; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Shaders the AMD driver compiled for DirectX games.
rules.whyBig: Each game adds compiled shaders.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; games recompile shaders, which can cause stutter at first.
rules.saferAlternative: AMD Software > Gaming > Graphics > Reset Shader Cache clears it.

rules.title: AMD DirectX 12 shader cache
rules.summary: Compiled DirectX 12 shaders from the AMD driver; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Shaders the AMD driver compiled for DirectX 12 games.
rules.whyBig: Each DirectX 12 game adds compiled shaders.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; games recompile shaders, which can cause stutter at first.
rules.saferAlternative: AMD Software > Gaming > Graphics > Reset Shader Cache clears it.

rules.title: AMD Vulkan shader cache
rules.summary: Compiled Vulkan shaders from the AMD driver; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Shaders the AMD driver compiled for Vulkan games and apps.
rules.whyBig: Each Vulkan game adds compiled shaders.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; games recompile shaders, which can cause stutter at first.

rules.title: AMD OpenGL shader cache
rules.summary: Compiled OpenGL shaders from the AMD driver; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Shaders the AMD driver compiled for OpenGL apps and games.
rules.whyBig: Each OpenGL app adds compiled shaders.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; shaders are recompiled.

rules.title: Intel graphics shader cache
rules.summary: Compiled shaders from the Intel graphics driver; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Shaders the Intel graphics driver compiled for games and apps.
rules.whyBig: Each game adds compiled shaders.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; shaders are recompiled, with stutter at first.

rules.title: Chrome profiles (User Data)
rules.summary: Browser profiles: history, passwords, extensions, cookies and caches
rules.whatItIs: All Chrome profiles (Default, Profile 1, ...) with bookmarks, history, saved passwords, cookies, extensions and site data, plus shared components and caches.
rules.whyBig: Caches, site storage (IndexedDB, service workers) and downloaded browser components such as on-device AI models make up most of it.
rules.ifDeleted: Every profile is reset: you are signed out of all sites, and history, passwords and extensions not synced to an account are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear browsing data from the browser (Settings > Privacy and security > Delete browsing data) or delete only the cache folders inside a profile.

rules.title: Chrome web cache
rules.summary: Cached web pages, images and scripts; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: The HTTP cache of one Chrome profile: copies of pages, images, video segments and scripts from sites you visited.
rules.whyBig: The browser fills it up to a size limit it picks from free disk space, which can be several GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; sites load a little slower until the cache refills. Close the browser first, as the files are in use.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear 'Cached images and files' in the browser (Settings > Privacy and security > Delete browsing data).

rules.title: Chrome compiled script cache
rules.summary: Compiled JavaScript and WebAssembly from visited sites; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Compiled versions of scripts from sites you visit, so they start faster next time.
rules.whyBig: It grows with the number of script-heavy sites and web apps you use, often hundreds of MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; scripts are compiled again on the next visit. Close the browser first.

rules.title: Chrome GPU shader cache
rules.summary: Compiled graphics shaders; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Shaders the browser compiled for your graphics card.
rules.whyBig: Usually small; it is rebuilt as needed.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; shaders are compiled again.

rules.title: Chrome offline site storage (service workers)
rules.summary: Offline copies stored by web apps; sites download them again
rules.whatItIs: Files that web apps (for example WhatsApp Web, Teams, Office and YouTube Music) store through service workers so they work offline and start fast.
rules.whyBig: Some web apps store hundreds of MB each and rarely clean up.
rules.ifDeleted: Sites download their files again on the next visit; offline use of those web apps stops until they do. Close the browser first.
rules.saferAlternative: To clear it per site, use the browser's site settings (Cookies and site data).

rules.title: Chrome site databases (IndexedDB)
rules.summary: Databases that websites store locally; may hold offline data
rules.whatItIs: Local databases that websites and web apps create, such as offline mail, drafts, chat history of web messengers, or web game saves.
rules.whyBig: Web apps that work offline can store hundreds of MB to GBs.
rules.ifDeleted: Sites lose their local data; anything not saved on the site's server (offline drafts, local saves) is lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove data per site in the browser's site settings instead of deleting the whole folder.

rules.title: Chrome on-device AI model
rules.summary: Chrome's built-in AI model (Gemini Nano); Chrome re-downloads it if the feature is on
rules.whatItIs: Chrome downloads a local AI model here for built-in AI features such as writing help and scam detection.
rules.whyBig: The model is several GB and is downloaded automatically on capable PCs.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks, but Chrome downloads it again while on-device AI features are enabled.
rules.saferAlternative: To keep it gone, turn off on-device AI in Chrome's settings (Settings > System), then delete the folder.

rules.title: Edge profiles (User Data)

rules.saferAlternative: Clear browsing data from the browser (Settings > Privacy, search, and services > Clear browsing data) or delete only the cache folders inside a profile.

rules.title: Opera profiles
rules.summary: Opera and Opera GX profiles: history, passwords, extensions and settings
rules.whatItIs: Opera's profile data (Opera Stable, Opera GX Stable) with bookmarks, history, passwords, cookies and extensions.
rules.whyBig: Site data and extensions grow with use; the web cache is kept separately in AppData\Local.
rules.ifDeleted: The browser is reset: you are signed out of sites and unsynced data is lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear browsing data from Opera's settings.

rules.title: Opera local data
rules.summary: Opera's local data, mostly caches
rules.whatItIs: Opera keeps its web cache and other local data for each edition (Opera Stable, Opera GX Stable) here.
rules.whyBig: The web cache grows to a size limit chosen by the browser.
rules.ifDeleted: Caches are rebuilt; close Opera first.

rules.title: Opera web cache
rules.summary: Cached web pages and images of Opera; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Opera's HTTP cache: copies of pages, images, video segments and scripts from sites you visited.
rules.whyBig: It fills up to a size limit the browser picks, which can be several GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; sites load a bit slower until the cache refills. Close Opera first.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear 'Cached images and files' from Opera's settings.

rules.title: Firefox profiles
rules.summary: Firefox profiles: bookmarks, history, passwords, extensions and site data
rules.whatItIs: Each subfolder is a Firefox profile with bookmarks, history, saved logins, cookies, extensions and site storage.
rules.whyBig: Site storage (the storage folder) and history databases grow with use; the web cache lives separately in AppData\Local.
rules.ifDeleted: Firefox starts with a blank profile; bookmarks, passwords and extensions not synced to a Mozilla account are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear site data in Firefox (Settings > Privacy & Security > Cookies and Site Data) instead.

rules.title: Firefox site storage
rules.summary: Data that websites store in Firefox (IndexedDB, offline caches)
rules.whatItIs: Local storage of websites: IndexedDB databases, offline caches of web apps and service worker data.
rules.whyBig: Web apps with offline support can store hundreds of MB to GBs.
rules.ifDeleted: Sites lose their local data; anything only saved locally (offline drafts, local web game saves) is lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Use Settings > Privacy & Security > Cookies and Site Data > Manage Data to remove data per site.

rules.title: Firefox cache
rules.summary: Firefox's disk cache and other rebuildable data; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: The local half of each Firefox profile: the web cache (cache2), start-up cache, thumbnails and safe-browsing lists. Your real profile is in AppData\Roaming.
rules.whyBig: The web cache grows to a size limit Firefox picks from free disk space, often 1 GB or more.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; Firefox rebuilds it. Close Firefox first.
rules.saferAlternative: Settings > Privacy & Security > Cookies and Site Data > Clear Data > Cached Web Content.

rules.title: Firefox crash reports
rules.summary: Crash reports of Firefox; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Crash reports Firefox created, sent or pending.
rules.whyBig: Each report can include a minidump of a few MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; unsent reports are not sent.

rules.title: Zen Browser profiles
rules.summary: Zen Browser profiles: bookmarks, history, passwords, extensions and site data
rules.whatItIs: Zen is based on Firefox; each subfolder is a profile with bookmarks, history, saved logins, cookies, extensions and site storage.
rules.whyBig: Site storage and history grow with use; the web cache lives in AppData\Local\zen.
rules.ifDeleted: Zen starts with a blank profile; unsynced bookmarks, passwords and extensions are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear site data from Zen's settings instead.

rules.title: Zen Browser cache
rules.summary: Zen Browser's disk cache; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: The local half of each Zen profile: web cache, start-up cache and thumbnails, as in Firefox.
rules.whyBig: The web cache grows to a size limit picked from free disk space.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the browser rebuilds it. Close Zen first.

rules.title: Discord program files
rules.summary: Discord app files; one app-* folder per installed version
rules.whatItIs: Discord installs per user here: Update.exe, app-<version> folders and downloaded update packages.
rules.whyBig: Each update adds a new app-<version> folder; older ones are usually removed after an update.
rules.ifDeleted: Discord stops working until reinstalled; your account data is on Discord's servers.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall from Installed apps if you do not use it.

rules.title: Discord data and caches
rules.summary: Discord settings, caches and downloaded modules
rules.whatItIs: Discord's settings, local storage, caches and the native modules it downloads after updates.
rules.whyBig: The web cache and code cache grow with images, videos and emojis you see.
rules.ifDeleted: You are signed out and the app downloads its modules and caches again.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear only the Cache and Code Cache folders while Discord is closed.

rules.title: Discord web cache
rules.summary: Cached images and files of the Discord app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: The HTTP cache of the Discord desktop app, which is built on Chromium: images, attachments previews and web resources it downloaded.
rules.whyBig: It grows with use, often to hundreds of MB or more.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; content is downloaded again. Quit Discord first, as the files are in use.

rules.title: Discord compiled script cache
rules.summary: Compiled JavaScript of the Discord app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Compiled scripts that the Discord app keeps so it starts faster.
rules.whyBig: Usually tens to hundreds of MB, and it can keep data from old app versions.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the app compiles its scripts again. Quit Discord first.

rules.title: Discord service worker cache
rules.summary: Offline web content cached by the Discord app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Files cached through service workers by the web views inside Discord.
rules.whyBig: It can grow to hundreds of MB over time.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the content is downloaded again. Quit Discord first.

rules.title: Slack data and caches
rules.summary: Slack settings, local data and caches
rules.whatItIs: Settings, local storage and Chromium caches of the Slack desktop app.
rules.whyBig: Caches of images and files from workspaces grow with use.
rules.ifDeleted: You are signed out of all workspaces; messages stay on Slack's servers.
rules.saferAlternative: Use Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache in Slack, or delete only the cache folders.

rules.title: Slack web cache
rules.summary: Cached images and files of the Slack app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: The HTTP cache of the Slack desktop app, which is built on Chromium: images, attachments previews and web resources it downloaded.

rules.title: Slack service worker cache
rules.summary: Offline web content cached by the Slack app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Files cached through service workers by the web views inside Slack.
rules.whyBig: It can grow to hundreds of MB over time.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the content is downloaded again. Quit Slack first.

rules.title: Microsoft Teams classic data
rules.summary: Cache and settings of classic Teams, which Microsoft has retired; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Caches, logs and settings of classic Microsoft Teams. Microsoft retired classic Teams in favour of the new Teams app, and its cache-clearing guidance deletes this folder's contents.
rules.whyBig: Caches of images, files and web resources, often several hundred MB, left behind after moving to the new Teams.
rules.ifDeleted: Classic Teams, if still installed, signs you out and rebuilds its cache. Chats and files stay in the cloud.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall 'Microsoft Teams classic' from Installed apps if it is still there.

rules.title: Microsoft Teams classic program files
rules.summary: Program files of classic Teams (retired); uninstall it from Installed apps
rules.whatItIs: The per-user installation of classic Microsoft Teams (current and previous versions, Update.exe).
rules.whyBig: Classic Teams kept the current and the previous version side by side.
rules.ifDeleted: Classic Teams stops working; it has been replaced by the new Teams.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall 'Microsoft Teams classic' from Installed apps.

rules.title: Spotify program files
rules.summary: Spotify desktop app files (non-Store install)
rules.whatItIs: The desktop version of Spotify installs its program files per user here.
rules.whyBig: The program itself is a few hundred MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Spotify stops working until reinstalled.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall from Installed apps.

rules.title: Spotify local data
rules.summary: Spotify's streaming cache and offline downloads
rules.whatItIs: Local data of the Spotify desktop app: its streaming cache (Storage) and songs downloaded for offline listening (Data).
rules.whyBig: The streaming cache can grow to many GB unless limited in Spotify's settings, plus offline downloads.
rules.ifDeleted: Cached songs stream again; offline downloads are lost and must be downloaded again.
rules.saferAlternative: In Spotify, use Settings > Storage to clear the cache or remove downloads.

rules.title: Spotify streaming cache
rules.summary: Spotify's streaming cache; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Pieces of songs and podcasts Spotify cached while streaming.
rules.whyBig: Spotify fills it up to a limit you can set in its settings, often several GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; songs stream again. Quit Spotify first.
rules.saferAlternative: In Spotify, use Settings > Storage > Clear cache.

rules.title: Spotify offline downloads
rules.summary: Songs and podcasts downloaded for offline listening
rules.whatItIs: Encrypted copies of the playlists, albums and podcasts you downloaded in Spotify.
rules.whyBig: Every downloaded playlist adds its songs at full quality.
rules.ifDeleted: Downloads are lost and must be downloaded again; nothing else breaks.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove downloads in Spotify (Settings > Storage > Remove all downloads).

rules.title: Zoom app and data
rules.summary: Zoom installs per user here: program files, settings and local chat data
rules.whatItIs: Zoom Workplace installs its program files (bin) per user here, together with settings, logs and local data.
rules.whyBig: The program plus logs and local data; recordings are saved to Documents\Zoom instead.
rules.ifDeleted: Zoom stops working until reinstalled and local settings are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall from Installed apps.

rules.title: Telegram Desktop
rules.summary: Telegram Desktop program, session and media cache
rules.whatItIs: The Telegram Desktop installer puts the program here; tdata holds your session and the cache of media you viewed.
rules.whyBig: Media from channels and groups is cached and can grow to many GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Telegram stops working and you are logged out of this device; cloud chats stay.
rules.saferAlternative: In Telegram, use Settings > Advanced > Manage local storage to clear the cache or set a limit.

rules.title: Telegram media cache
rules.summary: Cached photos, videos and files from Telegram chats
rules.whatItIs: Media Telegram Desktop downloaded while you browsed chats and channels.
rules.whyBig: Videos and files from busy channels add up quickly unless a cache limit is set.
rules.ifDeleted: Media from cloud chats is downloaded again when opened; media from secret chats is not recoverable.
rules.saferAlternative: Use Settings > Advanced > Manage local storage instead of deleting by hand. Quit Telegram first.

rules.title: OBS Studio settings
rules.summary: OBS scenes, profiles, plugins and logs
rules.whatItIs: Settings of OBS Studio: scene collections, profiles, plugin data, logs and crash reports. Recordings are saved to Videos by default.
rules.whyBig: Usually small; logs and crash reports accumulate.
rules.ifDeleted: OBS loses your scenes and profiles.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete old files in the logs and crashes subfolders if needed.

rules.title: Steam web cache
rules.summary: Cache of the Steam client's built-in browser; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Cache of the web pages shown inside the Steam client (store, community, library).
rules.whyBig: Store images and videos fill it over time, often hundreds of MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; Steam downloads the content again. Quit Steam first.
rules.saferAlternative: Steam > Settings > In Game/Web Browser > Delete Web Browser Data does the same.

rules.title: Epic Games Launcher data
rules.summary: Epic Games Launcher settings, logs and web cache
rules.whatItIs: Per-user data of the Epic Games Launcher: settings, logs and the cache of its built-in web views.
rules.whyBig: The web cache and logs grow over time.
rules.ifDeleted: The launcher loses its settings and you may need to sign in again.

rules.title: Epic Games Launcher web cache
rules.summary: Web cache of the Epic Games Launcher; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Cache of the store and library pages shown in the Epic Games Launcher.
rules.whyBig: Store images and videos fill it over time.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; Epic's support guidance clears it to fix launcher problems. Quit the launcher first.

rules.title: Epic Games Launcher logs
rules.summary: Launcher logs; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Log files of the Epic Games Launcher.
rules.whyBig: Logs accumulate over time.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks.

rules.title: Battle.net app data
rules.summary: Battle.net app settings, caches and logs
rules.whatItIs: Per-user data of the Battle.net app: account settings, browser caches and logs.
rules.whyBig: Browser caches and logs grow over time.
rules.ifDeleted: The app loses its local settings and signs you out.

rules.title: Battle.net cache
rules.summary: Cache of the Battle.net app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Cached data of the Battle.net app. Blizzard's troubleshooting steps delete it.
rules.whyBig: It grows with store content and updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the app rebuilds it. Quit Battle.net first.

rules.title: Battle.net browser cache
rules.summary: Web cache of the Battle.net app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Cache of the web pages shown inside the Battle.net app.
rules.whyBig: Store images and videos fill it over time.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the content is downloaded again. Quit Battle.net first.

rules.title: Battle.net logs
rules.summary: Battle.net app logs; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Log files of the Battle.net app.
rules.whyBig: Logs accumulate over time.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks.

rules.title: EA app data
rules.summary: EA app settings, logs and caches
rules.whatItIs: Per-user data of the EA app (formerly Origin): settings, logs and caches.
rules.whyBig: Logs and caches grow over time.
rules.ifDeleted: The EA app loses its settings and may ask you to sign in again.

rules.title: Ubisoft Connect data
rules.summary: Ubisoft Connect per-user logs and data
rules.whatItIs: Per-user data of Ubisoft Connect: logs and local state. Games and cached saves are in the launcher's install folder.
rules.whyBig: Usually small.
rules.ifDeleted: Ubisoft Connect loses local state; games are not affected.

rules.title: Riot Client data
rules.summary: Riot Client settings, logs and data
rules.whatItIs: Per-user data of the Riot Client: settings, logs and cached data.
rules.whyBig: Logs accumulate over time.
rules.ifDeleted: The Riot Client loses its settings and signs you out.

rules.title: Minecraft Java Edition
rules.summary: Minecraft Java: game files, mods, worlds (saves) and screenshots
rules.whatItIs: The Minecraft Java Edition folder: game versions, libraries and assets downloaded by the launcher, plus your worlds (saves), mods, resource packs and screenshots.
rules.whyBig: Every game version, modpack and world adds data; large worlds can be GBs.
rules.ifDeleted: Worlds and screenshots are lost; game files are downloaded again by the launcher.
rules.saferAlternative: Back up the saves folder; you can delete old versions in the versions folder.

rules.title: Minecraft worlds
rules.summary: Your Minecraft single-player worlds
rules.whatItIs: Each subfolder is a single-player world.
rules.whyBig: Worlds grow as you explore; large ones are GBs.
rules.ifDeleted: The worlds are gone for good unless backed up.

rules.title: Adobe app data (Roaming)
rules.summary: Settings and caches of Adobe apps
rules.whatItIs: Settings, presets and caches of Adobe apps (Creative Cloud, Premiere Pro, After Effects, Photoshop, Acrobat).
rules.whyBig: Media caches of video apps (Common\Media Cache Files) are usually the large part.
rules.ifDeleted: Adobe apps lose their settings and presets.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear media caches from inside the app (Premiere Pro: Settings > Media Cache > Delete).

rules.title: Adobe media cache files
rules.summary: Conformed audio and indexed media from Premiere/After Effects; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Files that Premiere Pro, After Effects and Media Encoder create when importing media: conformed audio (.cfa), indexes and accelerator files.
rules.whyBig: Every imported clip adds cache files, and they are never removed automatically unless you enable cleanup; tens of GB is common.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost from your projects; the apps rebuild what they need when media is next opened, which takes time.
rules.saferAlternative: In Premiere Pro, use Settings > Media Cache > Delete and turn on automatic deletion of old cache files.

rules.title: Adobe media cache database
rules.summary: Database that tracks Adobe media cache files; safe to clear with the cache
rules.whatItIs: The database Premiere Pro and After Effects use to track media cache files.
rules.whyBig: It grows with the number of imported clips.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost from your projects; the apps re-index media.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear it together with the media cache files from the app's Media Cache settings.

rules.title: Adobe audio waveform cache
rules.summary: Audio waveform (peak) files of Adobe video and audio apps; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Waveform data (.pek) that Premiere Pro and Audition generate to draw audio waveforms.
rules.whyBig: One file per imported audio stream.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; waveforms are regenerated.

rules.title: Adobe app data (Local)
rules.summary: Local data and caches of Adobe apps
rules.whatItIs: Local caches, logs and data of Adobe apps and Creative Cloud.
rules.whyBig: Font, library and app caches.
rules.ifDeleted: Adobe apps rebuild caches but may lose local state.

rules.title: Lightroom previews
rules.summary: Lightroom Classic preview cache; rebuilt when needed
rules.whatItIs: Standard and 1:1 previews Lightroom Classic renders for your catalog.
rules.whyBig: 1:1 previews of large RAW photos are several MB each, so a big catalog can have tens of GB.
rules.ifDeleted: No photos or edits are lost; Lightroom re-renders previews, which takes time. Close Lightroom first.
rules.saferAlternative: In Lightroom, use Library > Previews > Discard 1:1 Previews, and set automatic discarding in Catalog Settings.

rules.title: Lightroom smart previews
rules.summary: Smart Previews let you edit photos whose originals are offline
rules.whatItIs: Compressed DNG copies of photos that let you edit in Lightroom Classic when the originals are not connected.
rules.whyBig: Each smart preview is around 1 MB; large catalogs add up.
rules.ifDeleted: Photos whose originals are on a disconnected drive can no longer be edited until the drive is back.
rules.saferAlternative: In Lightroom, use Library > Previews > Discard Smart Previews for photos you do not need offline.

rules.title: Outlook offline mailbox (OST)
rules.summary: Offline copy of a mailbox; Outlook downloads it again from the server
rules.whatItIs: An offline cache of an Exchange, Microsoft 365 or IMAP mailbox in classic Outlook.
rules.whyBig: It holds as much of the mailbox as the 'download email for the past' setting allows, often many GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Outlook rebuilds it from the server, which takes time. Items that were not synced yet (for example drafts created offline) are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Reduce the offline period in Account Settings > Change > 'Download email for the past'.

rules.title: Outlook data file (PST)
rules.summary: Outlook archive or mailbox file; often the only copy of that mail
rules.whatItIs: An Outlook data file with mail, contacts and calendar items, used for archives and POP accounts.
rules.whyBig: Archives grow with every year of mail and attachments.
rules.ifDeleted: The mail in it is gone; PST files are often the only copy.
rules.saferAlternative: Open it in Outlook, delete or export what you do not need, then use File > Account Settings > Data Files > Settings > Compact Now.

rules.title: Office document cache
rules.summary: Office's cache of cloud documents; may hold edits not yet uploaded
rules.whatItIs: Cache that Office uses to open and sync documents stored in OneDrive and SharePoint.
rules.whyBig: Every cloud document you open adds a cached copy.
rules.ifDeleted: Edits that were not uploaded yet can be lost; otherwise documents are downloaded again.
rules.saferAlternative: In an Office app, use File > Options > Save > 'Delete cached files' after everything is synced.

rules.title: JetBrains system folders
rules.summary: JetBrains IDE caches, indexes, logs and Toolbox installs
rules.whatItIs: System folders of JetBrains IDEs (one per product and version, with caches, indexes, logs and local history) and, if used, Toolbox App installs.
rules.whyBig: Indexes of large projects, plus folders left from previous IDE versions after upgrades.
rules.ifDeleted: Caches and indexes are rebuilt, but local history is lost, and Toolbox-installed IDEs stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete folders of IDE versions you no longer use; recent IDEs also offer to clean up old directories themselves.

rules.title: JetBrains Toolbox and installed IDEs
rules.summary: Toolbox App and the IDEs it installed; uninstall IDEs from Toolbox
rules.whatItIs: The JetBrains Toolbox App and the IDEs it installed (apps), with their downloads and logs.
rules.whyBig: Each IDE is 1-3 GB, and Toolbox can keep previous versions for rollback.
rules.ifDeleted: The IDEs installed through Toolbox stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall IDEs or disable keeping previous versions in Toolbox's settings.

rules.title: JetBrains per-user installs (ReSharper)
rules.summary: Per-user JetBrains installs such as ReSharper and dotUltimate tools
rules.whatItIs: Per-user installations of JetBrains tools such as ReSharper and other .NET tools.
rules.whyBig: Each installed version is hundreds of MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Those tools stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall them with the JetBrains installer or Installed apps.

rules.title: JetBrains IDE system folder
rules.summary: Caches, indexes and local history of one JetBrains IDE version
rules.whatItIs: The system folder of one IDE version (for example Rider2025.3): caches, indexes, logs, local history and temporary files.
rules.whyBig: Indexes grow with the size of the projects you open; folders of old IDE versions stay after upgrades.
rules.ifDeleted: The IDE rebuilds caches and indexes (slow on large projects), but its Local History is lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete whole folders of versions you no longer use; for the current one, use File > Invalidate Caches.

rules.title: JetBrains IDE caches
rules.summary: IDE caches; rebuilt automatically
rules.whatItIs: Caches of a JetBrains IDE.
rules.whyBig: They grow with the projects you open.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the IDE rebuilds them on next start. Close the IDE first.
rules.saferAlternative: Use File > Invalidate Caches in the IDE.

rules.title: JetBrains IDE indexes
rules.summary: Code indexes of a JetBrains IDE; rebuilt automatically
rules.whatItIs: Indexes the IDE builds for code navigation and search.
rules.whyBig: They grow with the size of the projects and SDKs you open.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the IDE re-indexes, which can take a while on large projects. Close the IDE first.

rules.title: JetBrains IDE logs
rules.summary: IDE logs; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Log files of a JetBrains IDE.
rules.whyBig: Logs accumulate over time.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks.

rules.title: JetBrains IDE settings and plugins
rules.summary: IDE settings, plugins and scratch files
rules.whatItIs: Configuration folders of JetBrains IDEs (one per product and version): settings, installed plugins, keymaps and scratch files.
rules.whyBig: Plugins are the large part; old version folders stay after upgrades.
rules.ifDeleted: IDEs lose their settings, plugins and scratch files.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete folders of IDE versions you no longer use.

rules.title: Visual Studio user data
rules.summary: Visual Studio settings, extensions and caches for your account
rules.whatItIs: Per-user data of each Visual Studio instance: settings, per-user extensions, MEF component cache and logs.
rules.whyBig: Extensions and caches grow with use; folders for old Visual Studio versions remain.
rules.ifDeleted: Visual Studio loses settings and per-user extensions.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear only ComponentModelCache, or folders of Visual Studio versions you removed.

rules.title: Visual Studio component cache
rules.summary: Visual Studio's extension composition cache; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: The MEF component cache Visual Studio builds from installed extensions. Clearing it is a standard fix for extension load errors.
rules.whyBig: Usually tens of MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; Visual Studio rebuilds it at next start. Close Visual Studio first.

rules.title: Visual Studio telemetry buffer
rules.summary: Buffered telemetry of Visual Studio and VS Code tools; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Telemetry events that Microsoft developer tools buffer before sending.
rules.whyBig: Usually small; it can grow when sending fails.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks.

rules.title: TypeScript typings cache
rules.summary: Type definitions downloaded for editor IntelliSense; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Type definition packages that editors (VS Code, Visual Studio) download automatically to provide IntelliSense for JavaScript libraries.
rules.whyBig: One folder per TypeScript version with downloaded @types packages.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the editor downloads them again.

rules.title: VS Code user data
rules.summary: VS Code settings, workspace state, extension data and caches
rules.whatItIs: User data of Visual Studio Code: settings and keybindings (User), state of every opened workspace, extension data, backups of unsaved files and Chromium caches.
rules.whyBig: workspaceStorage grows with every folder you open, and extension data and caches add more.
rules.ifDeleted: VS Code loses settings, unsaved-file backups, local history and extension data. Settings Sync can restore settings.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear the cache folders (Cache, CachedData, CachedExtensionVSIXs, logs) and old workspaceStorage entries.

rules.title: VS Code web cache
rules.summary: Cached images and files of the VS Code app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: The HTTP cache of the VS Code desktop app, which is built on Chromium: images, attachments previews and web resources it downloaded.
rules.whyBig: It grows with use, often to hundreds of MB or more.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; content is downloaded again. Quit VS Code first, as the files are in use.

rules.title: VS Code compiled script cache
rules.summary: Compiled JavaScript of the VS Code app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Compiled scripts that the VS Code app keeps so it starts faster.
rules.whyBig: Usually tens to hundreds of MB, and it can keep data from old app versions.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the app compiles its scripts again. Quit VS Code first.

rules.title: VS Code service worker cache
rules.summary: Offline web content cached by the VS Code app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Files cached through service workers by the web views inside VS Code.
rules.whyBig: It can grow to hundreds of MB over time.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the content is downloaded again. Quit VS Code first.

rules.title: VS Code compiled code cache
rules.summary: Compiled code of current and previous VS Code versions; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Compiled JavaScript that VS Code caches per version to start faster.
rules.whyBig: Folders from previous VS Code versions stay after updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; VS Code rebuilds it on next start. Close VS Code first.

rules.title: VS Code extension package cache
rules.summary: Downloaded extension packages kept after install; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Extension packages (.vsix) that VS Code downloaded; installed extensions do not need them.
rules.whyBig: One package per installed or updated extension version.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; packages are downloaded again when needed.

rules.title: VS Code logs
rules.summary: VS Code and extension logs; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Log files of VS Code sessions and extensions.
rules.whyBig: One folder per session; some extensions log heavily.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks.

rules.title: VS Code workspace state
rules.summary: Per-folder state of VS Code and its extensions, including chat history
rules.whatItIs: One subfolder per folder or workspace you have opened, with editor state and extension data such as AI chat sessions, language server indexes and git data.
rules.whyBig: It grows with every folder you open and is not cleaned when those folders are deleted; some extensions store large indexes here.
rules.ifDeleted: VS Code forgets per-workspace state; extensions lose per-workspace data, for example chat history.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete subfolders of workspaces you no longer use (each contains a workspace.json naming its folder).

rules.title: VS Code extension data
rules.summary: Data that extensions store globally (downloads, indexes, sign-ins)
rules.whatItIs: Global storage of VS Code extensions: downloaded tools and language servers, caches, databases and state.
rules.whyBig: Some extensions download runtimes or models here.
rules.ifDeleted: Extensions lose their data and may download it again or need to be set up again.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove data of extensions you uninstalled.

rules.title: VS Code local history
rules.summary: Saved versions of files you edited (Timeline local history)
rules.whatItIs: VS Code's local history: earlier versions of files you edited, shown in the Timeline view.
rules.whyBig: Every save of every file adds an entry, up to the configured limits.
rules.ifDeleted: You lose the ability to restore earlier versions from the Timeline.

rules.title: VS Code unsaved file backups
rules.summary: Backups of unsaved editors (hot exit); may be your only copy
rules.whatItIs: Backups of files and untitled editors with unsaved changes, restored when VS Code starts again.
rules.whyBig: Usually small.
rules.ifDeleted: Unsaved changes and untitled editors are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Open VS Code and save or discard the restored editors instead.

rules.title: VS Code extensions
rules.summary: Installed VS Code extensions; uninstall them from the Extensions view
rules.whatItIs: Every installed VS Code extension, one folder per extension version.
rules.whyBig: Language extensions bundle runtimes and language servers (C++, Python, Java tools are hundreds of MB), and old versions can stay after updates.
rules.ifDeleted: The extensions disappear; VS Code can reinstall them from the Marketplace.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall unused extensions in VS Code's Extensions view.

rules.title: VS Code extensions folder
rules.summary: VS Code's extensions and start-up arguments
rules.whatItIs: Holds installed extensions and argv.json (start-up options) of VS Code.
rules.whyBig: Extensions are the large part.
rules.ifDeleted: Extensions and start-up options are lost.

rules.title: Cursor user data
rules.summary: Cursor editor settings, workspace state and caches
rules.whatItIs: User data of the Cursor editor (a VS Code fork): settings, workspace state, extension data and caches.
rules.whyBig: Workspace state and caches grow with use.
rules.ifDeleted: Cursor loses settings and per-workspace data.

rules.title: Cursor extensions
rules.summary: Installed Cursor extensions
rules.whatItIs: Extensions installed in the Cursor editor.
rules.whyBig: Language extensions bundle runtimes and language servers.
rules.ifDeleted: Extensions disappear and must be reinstalled.

rules.title: Per-user installed programs
rules.summary: Programs installed only for your account (no admin rights needed)
rules.whatItIs: Default location for programs installed per user, for example VS Code, Python, Ollama, Obsidian and many Electron apps.
rules.whyBig: Each program's full installation lives here.
rules.ifDeleted: Those programs stop working; uninstall them properly instead.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall programs from Settings > Apps > Installed apps.

rules.title: Per-user installer package cache
rules.summary: Cached installers needed to modify, repair or uninstall some programs
rules.whatItIs: Installer bundles (WiX Burn) cache their setup packages here for per-user installs, so the program can be repaired, changed or uninstalled later.
rules.whyBig: Each cached bundle keeps its packages, often tens to hundreds of MB.
rules.ifDeleted: The programs keep running, but repairing, upgrading or uninstalling them may fail or ask for the original installer.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall programs you do not need; their cached packages go with them.

rules.title: Connected Devices Platform data
rules.summary: Windows data for activity history and cross-device features
rules.whatItIs: Data of the Windows Connected Devices Platform service, used for activity history and features that link your PC with phones and other devices.
rules.whyBig: Usually small; activity databases can grow.
rules.ifDeleted: Activity history and device links reset; Windows recreates the folder.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear activity history in Settings > Privacy & security > Activity history.

rules.title: Windows Mail and Calendar data
rules.summary: Local data of the old Windows Mail and Calendar apps
rules.whatItIs: Local store (Unistore) of the Windows Mail and Calendar apps and related contact features.
rules.whyBig: Downloaded mail and attachments of accounts set up in the Mail app.
rules.ifDeleted: The Mail and Calendar apps lose their local data and re-sync accounts.

rules.title: VirtualStore (redirected writes)
rules.summary: Files old programs tried to write into Program Files or Windows
rules.whatItIs: When an older program without admin rights writes to Program Files or Windows, Windows silently redirects the write here (UAC virtualization).
rules.whyBig: Settings, saves or logs of old programs and games.
rules.ifDeleted: Those programs lose the settings or saves they think are in their install folder.
rules.saferAlternative: Check which program each subfolder belongs to before deleting it.

rules.title: Start menu tile placeholders
rules.summary: Placeholder logos for Start menu entries; tiny
rules.whatItIs: Placeholder images Windows uses for Start menu tiles and app entries.
rules.whyBig: Tiny.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; Windows recreates it.

rules.title: Shared Store app publisher data
rules.summary: Data shared between Store apps from the same publisher
rules.whatItIs: Shared storage that packaged apps from the same publisher use to exchange data.
rules.whyBig: Usually small.
rules.ifDeleted: Apps that share data through it may lose that data.

rules.title: Notification app icons
rules.summary: Icons cached for desktop app notifications; tiny
rules.whatItIs: Icons that desktop apps register for their Windows notifications.
rules.whyBig: Tiny.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; apps register their icons again.

rules.title: Squirrel installer temp
rules.summary: Temporary files of Squirrel-based installers (Discord, Slack, GitHub Desktop)
rules.whatItIs: Working folder of the Squirrel installer used by many Electron apps.
rules.whyBig: Interrupted installs and updates leave packages behind.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks.

rules.title: App updater download cache
rules.summary: Update installer downloaded by an Electron app; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Electron apps that use electron-updater (for example Obsidian, Notion, Bitwarden, Unity Hub) download their next update installer into a '<app>-updater' folder.
rules.whyBig: It holds one full installer, often 100-300 MB, sometimes left after the update was installed.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the app downloads the update again when it next checks.

rules.title: PowerShell package providers
rules.summary: Package providers for PowerShell (for example the NuGet provider)
rules.whatItIs: Provider assemblies used by PowerShell's Install-Module and Install-Package commands.
rules.whyBig: Tiny.
rules.ifDeleted: PowerShell asks to install the NuGet provider again.

rules.title: Cross-platform tool caches (.cache)
rules.summary: Caches of developer and AI tools that use the Unix-style .cache folder
rules.whatItIs: Folder used by cross-platform tools (Hugging Face, PyTorch, Puppeteer, pre-commit and others) for their caches, following the Unix XDG convention.
rules.whyBig: Downloaded AI models and browser builds are the usual large parts.
rules.ifDeleted: Most contents are re-downloaded when needed; some tools also keep login tokens here.
rules.saferAlternative: Check the subfolders; the known ones are explained individually.

rules.title: Cross-platform tool settings (.config)
rules.summary: Settings of developer tools that use the Unix-style .config folder
rules.whatItIs: Configuration folder of cross-platform tools (Git helpers, CLIs, editors) following the Unix XDG convention.
rules.whyBig: Usually small.
rules.ifDeleted: Tools lose their settings and sometimes stored logins.

rules.title: Cross-platform tool data (.local)
rules.summary: Programs and data of tools that use the Unix-style .local folder
rules.whatItIs: Folder used by cross-platform tools for installed binaries (.local\bin) and data (.local\share), following the Unix convention.
rules.whyBig: Tools installed here, such as some command-line apps, plus their data.
rules.ifDeleted: Tools installed here stop working.

rules.title: SSH keys and settings
rules.summary: Your SSH keys and known hosts; tiny, deleting locks you out of servers
rules.whatItIs: Your SSH private and public keys, client config and the list of known hosts.
rules.whyBig: A few KB.
rules.ifDeleted: You lose access to servers and Git hosts that use these keys unless you have copies.

rules.title: Claude Code data
rules.summary: Claude Code settings, memory, plugins and session transcripts
rules.whatItIs: Data of the Claude Code CLI: settings, instructions, installed plugins and skills, and transcripts of past sessions (projects).
rules.whyBig: Session transcripts in the projects folder accumulate with every session.
rules.ifDeleted: Claude Code loses settings, plugins and the ability to resume old sessions.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete old session transcripts in the projects folder if they are not needed.

rules.title: VirtualBox virtual machines
rules.summary: VirtualBox VMs: their disks, snapshots and settings
rules.whatItIs: Default folder for VirtualBox virtual machines: disk images (.vdi, .vmdk), snapshots and logs.
rules.whyBig: Each VM disk grows to the data stored inside it; snapshots add differencing disks.
rules.ifDeleted: The virtual machines and everything inside them are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove VMs in VirtualBox (Remove > Delete all files) and delete old snapshots there.
